# Results — Study 747 (Founder-Led-Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim — **"founder-led
firms outperform"** (Fahlenbrach 2009; Bain's "founder's mentality") — tested as a
textbook **long/short characteristic sort**: an equal-weighted **founder-led** basket
(long) minus a matched **professional-CEO** basket (short), rebalanced monthly. The
spread's **abnormal return** is the intercept (Jensen alpha) of a market-model regression
`r_LS = alpha + beta·SPY`, judged by a **Newey-West (HAC) t-stat**. There is no free
founder-CEO database, so the two baskets are a **hardcoded, transparent, hindsight-labelled
stand-in**; every input is a public price. Offline core + synthetic control are
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance monthly adjusted closes — each basket name + SPY (public, no key); adjusted = **total-return** proxy |
| Baskets | hardcoded `FOUNDER` / `PRO` membership, frozen at formation, fingerprint **c363d7e5e578** |
| As-of | 2026-07-13 (data through 2024-12; partial months dropped) |
| Formation | **2016-01** (membership frozen; no look-ahead re-selection) |
| Window | **108 months**, 2016-01 .. 2024-12 |
| Founder basket | 13 named; **11 priced** — `SQ` (reticker to XYZ) and `FIT` (delisted, acquired by Google 2021) drop out |
| Professional basket | 13 named, 13 priced |
| Model | market model / CAPM `r_LS = α + β·SPY`; Newey-West HAC SE (Bartlett, rule-of-thumb lags) |
| Rebalance / rf | monthly equal weight; risk-free set to 0 (near-zero for much of 2016–21), gross labelled gross |

> **The named caveat — survivorship, on the Signal axis, and it points *for* the claim.**
> The founder basket is the set of founder firms *salient in 2024* applied back to 2016 —
> a **hindsight / survivor-biased** sample. The founder-run flame-outs that delisted before
> 2024 (and never-listed disasters like Theranos) simply cannot enter it; two of our *own*
> originals (`SQ`, `FIT`) already dropped out for lack of a current series. This bias
> inflates the founder basket, so an **insignificant alpha here is a conservative
> refutation** — the true effect is, if anything, weaker than a survivor-tilted sample
> reports.

## The raw spread — the flattering headline (and it's real)

| basket | annualised (total-return proxy) |
|---|--:|
| **founder-led** (long) | **+34.5% / yr** |
| **professional-CEO** (short) | **+11.8% / yr** |
| **long/short (founder − professional)** | **+20.5% / yr** · **+156.5 bps/mo** · Sharpe **0.73** |

The raw long/short mean has a Newey-West HAC *t* of **+2.00** — which is exactly the trap:
the *raw* spread scrapes significance, so the believers stop here. The teardown is what
happens next.

## The abnormal return — CAPM alpha with a Newey-West HAC *t*

| series | alpha (bps/mo) | beta | HAC *t*(alpha) | R² |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **long/short** (founder − professional) | **+52.1** | **0.85** | **+0.76** | 0.26 |
| founder long-only | +50.6 | 1.62 | +0.84 | — |
| professional long-only | −1.5 | 0.77 | −0.09 | — |

**Decomposition of the raw spread:** `+156.5 bps = +52.1 alpha + +104.3 beta·E[mkt]` →
**67% of the "founder premium" is just market beta** (a high-beta tech long vs a low-beta
staples short in a decade-long bull market). The residual alpha — the only thing that could
be a *founder* effect — is **+52.1 bps/mo at *t* = 0.76**, indistinguishable from zero. Beta
is free; you can buy it in an index fund for basis points, so it is not a premium.

## Leave-one-out (jackknife) — the residual is one or two names

| dropped founder name | L/S alpha (bps/mo) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **NVDA** | **+21.9** | +0.33 |
| TSLA | +35.6 | +0.52 |
| SHOP | +37.6 | +0.58 |
| NFLX | +47.3 | +0.72 |
| META | +50.3 | +0.71 |
| AMZN | +51.4 | +0.73 |
| GOOGL | +52.3 | +0.72 |
| CRM | +54.8 | +0.77 |
| YELP | +62.6 | +0.82 |
| W | +72.8 | +1.11 |
| GPRO | +86.9 | +1.17 |

Dropping **NVDA alone** cuts the alpha from +52.1 to **+21.9 bps** (*t* = 0.33); dropping
the *duds* (GoPro, Wayfair, Yelp) **raises** it. A characteristic premium would barely move
when you remove one name — this one lives in a handful of rockets, the signature of a
concentration artefact, not a repeatable factor.

## Placebo — the founder *label* isn't even special

Shuffle the founder/professional labels across the **same pooled names** 4,000 times and
recompute the L/S alpha:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed founder-tag alpha | +52.1 bps/mo |
| random-label null mean | +0.4 bps/mo |
| two-sided *p* | **0.331** |
| random split reaches the founder alpha | **16%** of the time |

Given these very names, a *random* long/short split does as well as the real founder
labelling 16% of the time (*p* = 0.33). The founder *tag* adds nothing beyond
basket-membership luck. (This null isolates the label; it does not undo the hindsight
selection of the pool itself — that bias is named separately above and points the same way.)

## Costs + short borrow — not the binding constraint

| | monthly |
|---|--:|
| gross L/S | +156.5 bps |
| net (10 bps one-way turnover both legs + 300 bps/yr borrow on the short) | **+128.5 bps** |
| total drag | 28.0 bps |

Costs barely dent it (net ≈ gross): the founder premium is **not** killed by frictions, it
is killed by **asking where it came from** (beta + survivorship). That is why the verdict is
Mirage on tradability rather than Fragile.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic two-basket panel (higher founder beta, matched idiosyncratic noise) with a
**plantable founder alpha**:

| planted founder alpha | L/S alpha (bps/mo) | HAC *t* | beta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps/mo** (no edge) | +25.2 | **+0.82** | 0.24 |
| **+200 bps/mo** (large) | +225.2 | **+7.29** | 0.24 |

With **no** planted edge the L/S alpha stays comfortably below *t* = 2 (no false positive,
even with a beta gap present); a **+200 bps/mo** plant is recovered cleanly at *t* = 7.3. The
control proves the machinery separates alpha from beta and won't manufacture a premium — so
the real-tape alpha *t* of **0.76** is exactly what *no founder edge* looks like through this
lens.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The market-model alpha is **+52.1 bps/mo at Newey-West *t* = 0.76** —
  zero, statistically. **67%** of the raw +156.5 bps spread is beta; the placebo says the
  founder label isn't special (*p* = 0.33); the jackknife says the residual is one name (drop
  NVDA ⇒ +21.9 bps, *t* = 0.33). Literature support plus a survivor-tilted sample that
  *still* can't clear *t* = 2 ⇒ **NONE**, not even WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The basket is **hindsight-selected** — formed from the answer
  key — and could not have been built ex-ante; two originals (SQ, FIT) delisted outright. The
  net +128.5 bps is mostly free beta plus an insignificant, one-name residual. Nothing
  harvestable at any size.
- **"Founder premium?" — MISATTRIBUTED.** The raw outperformance is **real** and
  **mis-explained**: it is survivorship (only the winners are remembered) and tech-sector beta
  concentrated in ~2 names — not a leadership characteristic you can screen for and harvest.
